bystander_note: The bystander rule of trial_workers_v4.json (approach_m = hri_control.json drive.junction_slow_radius_m 3.0; nearer_margin_m 1.0): every worker of a node at least 1.0 m farther from the robot than the node's first worker at every point of the last 3.0 m of the arrival road (the start node: the start position).
random_note: PENDING ANISHA AND NUSRAT (experiments_ab.md section 3, conflict found by the first test): with Anisha's 6 m x 6 m square (scenarios_ab.json half_size_m 3.0) and the 1.0 m bystander margin, 3 workers at J1 can practically never be placed (0 of 200 000 draws) and 2 need about 11 800; the random layout uses a 0.25 m margin (every other worker still strictly farther than the first along the approach; about 114 draws for 2 workers, 2 900 for 3), up to 100 000 seeded draws. Alternatives: 1.0 m with a 10 m square, or no third worker at J1 in A4 and B4.
ask_note: The worker who answers a new ask: the active worker within 3.5 m of the pan-tilt camera (approach 2.0 m + margin; workers stand at least 3.0 m apart) with the smallest horizontal angle between the camera's forward axis and the direction to the worker (Python pans the camera to the person it asks).
answer_zone_note: 2026-11-17, experiments_ab.md section 15 addendum 1, item 3a (declared before the change): the worker chosen by the rule above answers only while the robot's centre is within 6.0 m of the worker's own node; outside it the worker is the commander but shows nothing (truth NONE). 6.0 m: zones of two asking nodes never overlap (2 x 6.0 < 12.5 m, the shortest node spacing of any map) and the modelled ask positions of a node's own workers (first ask and second opinions) lie within 5.5 m (live slots: up to 5.40 m at J1). It does not cover a robot that Python drives into another node's zone (A3 run 1 at 159 s, 4.7 m from J2): that needs Python's second-opinion search to stay near its node.
clearance_note: 2026-11-17, experiments_ab.md section 15 addendum 1, item 3b (declared before the change). No worker within path_clearance_m 1.0 m (Python's person-in-path corridor half-width 0.6 m, hri_control.json safety.corridor_half_width_m, + 0.4 m) of any segment the robot can drive: every road of the run's map and of the physical v4 map; per asking node, from the node to the ask position of each of its workers in every order (second opinions) and back to the first (tie); from every ask position and re-ask point to the next node of every branch. Ask position = ask_standoff_m from the worker toward where the robot comes from; re-ask point = reask_shift_m to the robot's right, back on that circle (copies of Python's hri_control.json dialog.approach_distance_m and of the v4 controller's configs/v4/control.json dialog.reask_shift_m, 0.8 m, which overrides v3's 0.4 m; corrected 2026-11-17, section 15 addendum 3: the first copy took v3's 0.4 m). Every modelled ask position lies within answer_zone_radius_m - answer_zone_margin_m (5.5 m) of its node. Both checks apply only while clearance_layout is active.

clearance_layout.note: ACTIVE since 2026-11-18 (experiments_ab.md section 15 addendum 4, declared before the change; Nusrat's decision after Anisha's PR #42, AUDIT.md 16.21.2): layout (i) of addendum 3, two workers at every asking node in every experiment, slot 1 3.0 m before and 2.0 m left, slot 2 2.5 m AHEAD and 4.0 m right; the live junction_slots and three_worker_nodes above carry the same values; the clearance and ask-zone checks apply at Play. Unity's planner places every run of seeds 1 and 2 of the 10 settings under every rule (ExperimentClearanceTests). The record below is the block before the switch: its slots were (3.5, -2.5), (-4.5, 3.5), (-5.0, -4.0) with two_worker_experiments A4, B4. PENDING ANISHA (2026-11-17, Nusrat's choice; experiments_ab.md section 15 addendum 1, item 3b). The corner layout that keeps the clearance on every map: slot 1 3.5 m before and 2.5 m left of the junction, slot 2 4.5 m AHEAD and 3.5 m right, slot 3 (J1 in A3, B3) 5.0 m ahead and 4.0 m left; start slots unchanged; A4 and B4 with 2 workers at J1 (3 random workers in the 6 m square cannot keep the clearance). Found by a geometry search over every slot on a 0.5 m grid (smallest largest own-ask distance, 5.19 m, then least movement from the section 3 slots), under the declared segment model including the return to the first worker (tie); the first search left the tie out and its choice (slot 1 2.5 m before, slot 3 3.5 m left) failed the Unity check by 0.03 m (section 15 addendum 1, record of item 3b). Stays inactive until Anisha's scenarios_ab.json (junction_slots, people_by_node of scenario 4), her MatchesUnity tests and her simulator's placement carry it; then active becomes true in one change and junction_slots / three_worker_nodes above are replaced by these values. 2026-11-17, section 15 addendum 3: WITH THE V4 RE-ASK SHIFT (0.8 m) THESE SLOTS FAIL with three workers at J1 (an ask point 5.51 m from J1) and with two at J1 on roadmap (slot 2 0.84 m from a drive); no beside slot set with three at J1 keeps every rule, nor do three random workers at J1. Kept unchanged and inactive until Nusrat and Anisha decide between the alternatives of addendum 3.

checkpoints.note: 2026-11-18, experiments_ab.md section 15 addendum 6 (variant T4, declared before the change): one checkpoint worker beside each listed decision branch (s_m along the branch from its junction, right_m to the right of the travel direction, negative = left); positions = addendum 5 item 3c proposals that meet P1-P10 and Q1-Q2 (checkpoint_feasibility_v4_20261118_214624). J1 LEFT -> J2 and J2 FORWARD -> J4 have no valid spot: the next junction honest workers point BACK there (ExperimentPlanAB.TruthfulCommand, unchanged); Unity refuses a run whose map has a decision branch with neither. Same template and navigation looks as every worker; honest PROCEED on a branch toward B, POINT back toward its junction otherwise; a liar (the set lie_probability, per worker per run, seeded) shows the opposite. Answers only while the road nearest the robot centre is its branch and the robot is within answer_radius_m of it (else NONE). Fixed; every node worker is placed around the checkpoints under every rule, and each checkpoint is checked under every rule. second_opinion_radius_m is a copy of configs/v4/control.json lie_detection.second_opinion_radius_m (pinned by CheckpointWorkersTests).

markers_note: Ground-truth stand rings (GroundTruth layer, never in a robot camera): green for a truthful worker, magenta-red for a liar; the ask markers of RunVisualsV4 get the answering worker's colour as an outer ring.
